parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence and no documented targeting of gender-nonconforming people; no facility, custody or border rule reaches visitors. But the picture is adverse beyond the dead-letter statute: police actively use Article 331 as an extortion lever against people perceived as gay (a documented tier-2 lever that plausibly reaches visibly trans visitors), NGOs report harassment, physical violence and financial extortion by state and non-state actors, and there is no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse. Social attitudes are hostile (73% would dislike a homosexual neighbour — sexuality-framed, so trans-specific attitudes are unmeasured and extrapolated from a hostile LGB climate). Violence findings are qualitative with no denominators, so they are pattern evidence, not campaign evidence. Tier-3 hostility with thin recourse plus a documented police extortion practice sits between elevated and high risk: no universal-exposure rule or organised sweeps keeps it out of 0.35, but the combination of real police misuse, hostility and no statutory recourse holds it at the lower elevated band.
